leadership-development.title: Leadership Development
leadership-development.intro: CORE’s source site describes an age-appropriate leadership curriculum focused on character strengths, emotional intelligence, decision-making, and growth mindset.
leadership-development.detail: This legacy page says the after-school curriculum is facilitated two hours each week and also describes an Emerging Leaders Lab offered at West Prep Academy for students identified with leadership potential.

sections.heading: After-school leadership curriculum
body: The source page connects self-control, curiosity, gratitude, empathy, decision-making, and emotional intelligence with stronger academic and life outcomes.

sections.heading: Emerging Leaders Lab
body: The page describes an in-school enrichment class at West Prep Academy where selected students learn from guest speakers, perform community service, and pursue leadership opportunities inside and outside school.

community-service.title: Community Service & Service Learning
community-service.intro: Community service gives Scholars a way to connect learning, responsibility, empathy, and real-world impact.
community-service.detail: CORE Scholars work with nonprofits and community organizations to identify needs, develop service projects, and reflect on how their actions strengthen the community.

sections.heading: Service learning
body: CORE frames service as more than volunteer hours. Scholars connect classroom learning to community needs while practicing teamwork, communication, compassion, responsibility, and confidence.

sections.heading: Annual service commitment
body: The current Character Development page states that each Scholar completes 50 hours of community service annually.

career-we-can.title: Career We Can
career-we-can.intro: Career We Can is CORE’s exploration and pathways program, launched in 2018.
career-we-can.detail: The current site describes internships, workplace exposure, mentoring, guest speakers, and hands-on experiences designed to help Scholars discover career fields and prepare for the future.

sections.heading: Mentor our Scholars
body: Career We Can mentors work with groups of Scholars to explore career pathways, set goals, identify actions, and make decisions that move those goals forward.

sections.heading: Inspire our Scholars
body: Professionals can share their life and career journey as guest speakers, including the obstacles they have navigated and what helped them succeed.

sections.heading: Host our Scholars
body: Organizations can open their workplaces to students for guided tours, employee panels, job shadowing, and other career-exploration experiences.

sections.heading: Partner voice
body: “I enjoyed the interaction with the kids. Sharing my stories with them was amazing. I decided to get involved with Career We Can because I want to help inspire our next generation and allow them to see greatness in themselves.”
sections.quote: Vincent Rotolo, Founder of Good Pie

social-emotional-learning.title: Social Emotional Learning (SEL)
social-emotional-learning.intro: SEL helps young people understand and manage emotions, make responsible decisions, maintain healthy relationships, and show empathy.
social-emotional-learning.detail: CORE’s source page presents SEL as a practical toolkit for navigating challenges, strengthening confidence, and improving well-being.

sections.heading: Understanding yourself
body: SEL can help students recognize what they are feeling, understand why, and choose healthier responses.

sections.heading: Building stronger relationships
body: Listening, empathy, and effective communication can deepen relationships with friends, family, and community.

sections.heading: Navigating challenges
body: Problem-solving, persistence, and treating mistakes as learning opportunities help students move through difficulty.

sections.heading: Developing empathy
body: Seeing situations from different perspectives can strengthen kindness, inclusion, and care for others.

two-generational.title: Two-Generational Approach
two-generational.intro: CORE’s two-generation approach recognizes that the well-being and success of children and parents are closely connected.
two-generational.detail: The source site describes supporting both generations at the same time: helping parents access education, training, employment, housing, health, and other resources while supporting Scholars’ educational, social, and emotional development.

sections.heading: Support parents and children together
body: Two-generation programs address immediate barriers and long-term opportunity across the household rather than treating student needs in isolation.

sections.heading: Pathways for parents
body: The current source page names education, job training, housing, healthcare, mental-health support, and other resources as examples of support that can improve employment prospects, stability, and well-being.

sections.heading: Development for Scholars
body: By investing in educational, emotional, and social development, CORE aims to help students build a stronger foundation for future success.

sections.heading: Stronger family connections
body: The page emphasizes positive relationships, family bonds, and a ripple effect across generations.
